$description: Shingō 信号 design tokens (industrial print system). Source of truth for web/shingo.css and ios/Sources/ShingoKit/SGTheme.swift.

color.$note: Two-ink screen print. Dark = bone print on ink stripes; light = ink print on sage stripes. Plates are solid print with knocked-out text (sage-* = print, ink = ground). Coral is the only extra ink.

roles.ground-hi: the print: titles, line art, plates of text
roles.sage-hi: solid print plates you press or carry
roles.ink: text knocked out of a plate (= ground)
roles.signal-text: coral used as text: full coral on ink, deep coral on sage for legibility
roles.signal-plate: coral as text inside a print plate (the plate flips the ground): deep coral on bone plates, full coral on ink plates

display.use: display wordmarks, 34 pt and up: wide and short

readout.use: timers, counters, hero numbers; wide cells, no ghosts

typeScale.$note: Anybody at three widths. Display 40+ extra-expanded 800, titles 28 expanded 800, inline 14 expanded 700. Wide and short: never condensed or rounded.

cuts.$note: 45° chamfers cut top-left + bottom-right, so every cut line runs '/'

geometry.radius: none (radar rings and the device frame only)

rules: Two inks: print and ground only. Plates are solid print with knocked-out text. Coral is the single extra ink.
One angle, one direction: every diagonal rises left to right at 45°; cuts sit top-left and bottom-right. No tilts, textures, shadows or rounding (device chrome excepted).
Wide, short, hard type: Anybody at three widths, Saira Stencil One for serials, IBM Plex Mono for telemetry.
Two tiers: poster screens compose freely; every other screen follows the screen grammar.
One signal per screen: one coral block or primary action, plus small states.
Shapes come from the alphabet or from the screen's own subject (tumblers, barbs, DIP switches…), drawn by the same rules.
No pictorial scenes: no photography, no illustrated or generated cities. Imagery comes from the shape system (backdrops, motifs, diagrams).
Every screen ships in both modes. Use role tokens, never raw hex.
Language: English runs the interface; Japanese and French are accents, at most once each per screen; all three stack once per app.
States have shapes: nominal = solid square, caution = hatch, fault = coral X, offline = dim X, syncing = marching hatch. Never colour alone.
Data is a spec sheet: coded columns, row index, tabular figures, coral bar on the selected row. Checkboxes are X boxes, radios diamonds, steppers cut keys.
The machine reports: notifications type in like a telex; loading is drafting hatch that slides continuously, never shimmer or spinner.
Beyond the phone: larger screens keep the grammar and add a rail (masthead, readout hero, spec-table body, selection side panel, imprint + ticker).

tiers.utility: masthead → hero → divider → body → imprint, on one backdrop
tiers.poster: launch, onboarding, lock screen, empty state, relay city: free composition

screenGrammar.masthead: vertical micro-code + title (28) + exactly one tag (vertical Japanese, a hanko, short meta or one action), then a span rule "value ──── value"
screenGrammar.hero: at most one form: a scene, a scope, a readout, a plate, a motif from the screen's subject, or chevrons
screenGrammar.divider: hazard for system and safety screens, tick ruler for data, slash run for money and content
screenGrammar.body: print on the ground: rows with ground-3 hairlines, wide-caps group labels over a print rule, notched frames for grouped data; solid plates only for things you press or carry
screenGrammar.imprint: print rule, wide-caps line, mono reference, barcode
screenGrammar.backdrop: one tonal composition per screen, chosen by subject (see the gallery backdrop sheet)
screenGrammar.coral: one signal block or one primary action per screen, plus the latest or active state; coral text uses signal-text
screenGrammar.languages: Japanese in the masthead tag or a seal; French in the span rule or fine print; one of each at most

instruments.seg7: seven-segment readout · timers, counters, hero numbers
instruments.ruler: tick-scale slider with a coral needle
instruments.stamp: worn stencil stamp · verified, sealed, void
instruments.ticket: notched, perforated stub · passes, receipts, plans
instruments.keycap: physical push button with LED · the one mechanical action
instruments.dataplate: riveted nameplate with dot-leader specs and matrix code
instruments.marks: crop marks, registration target, palette colour bar
instruments.bootlog: terminal loading lines with coral caret + marching hazard
instruments.blueprint: 24/6 pt grid ground for edit modes

motion.timing: never eased. Slides (tickers, marching hazard/hatch, wipe band) are continuous and linear; state changes (blinks, fills, pulses, sweep, decode) are stepped; none under reduced motion

scramble.noise: class-keeping: digits→0–9, capitals→X K Z N R V H E W # /, lower→x k z n r v h e w # /, kanji→信号経路保護暗中封鎖; punctuation and spaces never scramble
scramble.lock: per-character random lock time; frames every 28–80 ms; 45% flicker per frame

triggers.arrival: region enters view: titles, then labels (+90 ms), then data (+180 ms), 18 ms stagger, capped at 700 ms
triggers.change: a value's text changes (stepper, selected row, telex time, HUD callout, [data-decode-change])
triggers.touch: pointer enters a button, keycap, tab, rail item, chip or segment

scramble.never: paragraphs, inputs, tickers, telex messages, seven-segment readouts, [data-no-decode]

motion.wipe: hazard band on the diagonal, slides linearly over 520 ms, coral leading edge
motion.readouts: countdowns 1 s, counters ~1.4 s, coordinates drift 1.6 s
motion.hud: coral brackets (9 pt) + coral callout, snapped to the data element

patterns.$note: Patterns for any app. Web classes in web/shingo.css; SwiftUI in SGPatterns.swift.

shapes.fault: hard X, coral; label in signal-text

specTable.web: .stable (thead th > small code), td.idx, td.n, tr[aria-selected=true]
specTable.selected: ground-2 fill + 4 px coral bar on the left
specTable.columns: codes C-01…, wide caps titles, tabular figures

skeleton.motion: hatch slides continuously, linear, seamless loop

console.grid: 72 px rail · fluid main · 320 px side; rows 76 top · auto KPIs · main · 58 foot

monoliths.$note: Grand backdrops: one oversized hard mass per screen, bleeding off every edge, printed quietly in the stripe's own tone: mass = ground-2, secondary = ground-2 at 50%, openings = holes (even-odd) showing the stripes, small cuts = ground. No outlines, no ground-3. Level, upright or '/' edges (X, chevrons, diamond excepted). Source: tools/monoliths.py; web #g-bg-<name>; iOS SGMonolith.

kinds.bulkhead: blast doors on a / seam · passcode
kinds.giant-x: the mark at building scale · alert
kinds.cells: a meter at building scale · interval timer
kinds.notch-plate: notch frame as a mass · template
